Population.evidence_source: With regard to the health care received, from admission to the emergency ward and transfer to the psychiatric ward, patients' opinions were quite similar. Overall, they appreciated the effectiveness and availability of health care providers and the adequacy of 'standard' care, meaning admission to hospital and pharmacological therapy: I found the level of assistance was good but I feel a deep sense of uncertainty about the future . . . also because I haven't yet been given effective treatment . . . (M) . . . I had a positive impression . . . I had a good relationship with the staff, the nurses . . . (F)

Type.evidence_source: With regard to the health care received, from admission to the emergency ward and transfer to the psychiatric ward, patients' opinions were quite similar.

Area.evidence_source: It has been noticed, though, how both medical and nursing staff may show problems relating to patients, because of a poor understanding of the suffering behind suicide attempt, which results in attitudes of blame and stigmatization towards patients. The lack of health care professionals' empathy was underlined as the most problematic in 'standard' care: There were not many suggestions from patients about assistance options, which shows how uncommon it is for them to be listened to and be allowed to make critical suggestions; where suggestions were made, however, they were fitting and ranged from non-pharmacological treatment targeting emotional containment, to working through the attempt from a psychological point of view and to the creation of therapeutic spaces where one can feel 'understood'. The patients underlined the importance of sharing the suicide attempt experience with other people going through the same experience, as in the focus groups, and suggested the creation of self-help groups (no one had had experience of such groups before) led by a health care provider:
